content.title: About
content.content: Dry enriched spaghetti pasta is made from durum wheat and fortified with vitamins and minerals (iron, thiamine, niacin, folic acid). It has the classic long cylindrical shape, cooks quickly, and holds its texture after boiling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Spaghetti is one of the most popular pasta shapes worldwide, especially in Italy and the United States.
Fortification of pasta with vitamins and minerals began in the mid‑20th century to improve the nutritional quality of the diet.
Durum wheat gives pasta a firmer structure and a lower glycemic index compared with soft wheat.
Traditionally, spaghetti is cooked "al dente," meaning it remains slightly firm in the center.
Dry pasta can be stored for up to 2–3 years in a cool, dry place.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Spaghetti provides a steady release of energy thanks to slowly digestible carbs.

items.title: Enriched with B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, niacin and folic acid support metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron is essential for hemoglobin formation and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Dry pasta contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Provides plant protein
items.content: Spaghetti supplies about 13 % protein by dry weight, beneficial for vegetarians.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat pasta contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic load if overeaten
items.content: Large portions can raise blood sugar quickly, especially in individuals with diabetes.

items.title: Added salt in sauces
items.content: Spaghetti is often served with salty sauces, which can increase sodium intake.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, add the pasta and cook 8–10 minutes until "al dente." Drain, optionally rinse with cold water, then serve with sauce, vegetables or meat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry spaghetti in a sealed package in a cool, dry, dark place. After opening, transfer to an airtight container to keep out moisture and pests.
